records.title: Continuum timing in Proba-3 solar images
records.summary: In one September orbit, all 63 flagged Fe XIV products used a different-cycle continuum exposure with a smaller representative-time lag than either same-cycle donor, despite similar exposure-start lags. A ten-image sensitivity test found small sign changes under a bracketing continuum substitution.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: A magnetic "hole" in the solar wind reached Earth (6 Oct 2023)
records.summary: Three spacecraft saw the magnetic field drop for about half an hour inside a known solar eruption, and the matching pressure pulse arrived at Earth on schedule.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: A solar magnetic structure reached the inner spacecraft last (28–29 Sep 2023)
records.summary: A structure seen by Wind has a candidate counterpart at STEREO-A that arrived hours later, even though STEREO-A was closer to the Sun.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: Opposite magnetic directions in the solar wind at the same time (31 Jan 2019)
records.summary: ACE and DSCOVR measured a northward field for a full hour while Wind measured southward. Two probes near the Moon then sided with ACE and DSCOVR.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: Two solar eruptions short of carbon (June 2003)
records.summary: Near Jupiter's distance from the Sun, Ulysses found two catalogued eruptions strongly depleted in fully ionized carbon and rich in helium.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: A candidate source for the far-side solar eruption of 13 July 2021
records.summary: Of the numbered regions tested, NOAA 12849 lies closest to the observed X-ray direction. The above-limb centroid leaves the source longitude uncertain.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: The strongest oxygen-ion signal of 2011 in the solar wind
records.summary: Wind's measurement on 29 September 2011 stands. A link to debris from comet Elenin was tested and remains uncertain.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: Parker Solar Probe's radio data depend on an instrument setting
records.summary: Inside Venus's shadow, the probe's radio power rose with its antenna bias current, an effect users of these data need to correct for.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: Faster solar eruptions bring a storm's peak sooner
records.summary: Across 113 severe magnetic storms from 1996 to 2025, the storm peaked about 11 hours after the shock wave reached Earth when the eruption was fast, and about 23 hours after when it was slow. This is a pattern in past storms, not a forecasting tool.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: Cosmic-ray dips alone do not forecast magnetic storms
records.summary: In 1963–2000, sudden drops in cosmic rays were followed by severe storms slightly more often than chance. The excess did not hold up in the 2001–2016 test period. The catalogue's event classes already record whether a shock arrived, which would contaminate any forecast built on them.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: A lightning gamma-ray flash seen from two directions (20 Mar 2016)
records.summary: Fermi and AGILE recorded the same thunderstorm flash over Borneo from directions 93° apart.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: Two fireballs 2.3 seconds apart over the Pacific (21 Nov 2023)
records.summary: The lightning cameras on two GOES weather satellites resolve two separate fireballs about 315 km apart.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: Fireballs recorded by instruments on the ground
records.summary: The Sims Corner fireball (Washington, 14 Aug 2026) and an Interior Alaska fireball (1 Jan 2022) left matching signals in seismometers and pressure sensors. Satellites place Sims Corner's brightest flash about 32 km up.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: Four meteors in under nine seconds (24 Aug 2026)
records.summary: Four meteors over Germany and Denmark appeared to come from nearly the same point in the sky. A chance grouping is still possible.
records.topic: The Sun, space weather and Earth's sky

records.title: Mali’s Inner Niger Delta shows a delayed seasonal flood wave (2024–26)
records.summary: On two same-track SWOT RiverSP D July–January comparisons, Diré stood 4.64 m and 3.55 m higher while Mopti changed by no more than 0.18 m. Independent gauges and a second altimeter corroborate the stage contrasts; a persistent change in discharge was not established.

records.title: A one-day pulse of red-reflecting water in the northern Adriatic (6 Nov 2025)
records.summary: NASA's PACE satellite, an offshore tower instrument and Europe's Sentinel-3 all saw the shelf water brighten in red light for a day and fade the next; PACE measured a 56% drop at 620 nm. Stirred-up or passing particles are plausible, the cause is unresolved, and similar events appear in earlier observations.

records.title: Two Apollo 17 eclipse windows showed no compelling moonquake excess
records.summary: The event counts were compared with uneclipsed full Moons and adjacent windows. A separate test of deep moonquake sources found no unusual pairing. Recording coverage and detection efficiency limit both tests.

records.title: One lunar crater counted twice
records.summary: Two catalogue entries describe the same 9-metre impact crater. Additional orbiter images halve the window in which it formed, to 177 days.

records.title: Martian "repeat impacts" checked against spacecraft images
records.summary: One apparent repeat is a duplicated catalogue entry. Another is two real craters 2.26 km apart that formed at least 115 days apart.

records.title: Neighbouring Martian craters come in similar sizes
records.summary: Across 259 fresh impact fields, nearby craters are more alike in size than chance predicts. A model of meteors breaking up in the atmosphere explains only part of the pattern.

records.title: Two NASA gravity maps of Mars differ mostly in where they put zero longitude
records.summary: The 2020 and 2026 models use prime meridians about 100 metres apart on the ground (6.07 arcseconds). Rotating one to match the other removes about 99% of their apparent large-scale difference, which is not a change in Mars itself.

records.title: Perseverance sensed Phobos passing beside the Sun
records.summary: Sky sensors on the rover dimmed by up to about 2% when the moon passed close to, but not across, the Sun.

records.title: A candidate Mars Trojan and a possible temporary companion of Earth
records.summary: Asteroid 2026 RF64 appears to trail Mars along its orbit. A second object may briefly accompany Earth.

records.title: Phobos's shadow will touch Deimos three times (8, 9 and 11 Oct 2027)
records.summary: Predicted Phobos penumbral shadows on Deimos in October 2027

records.title: Energetic particles surged in Mars orbit (22–29 Aug 2025)
records.summary: NASA's MAVEN orbiter recorded peak hourly median fluxes on 24 August, about 5,140 times the survey reference for ions and 24,450 times for electrons. Forecasts for two solar eruptions fit the timing.

records.title: Phobos will hide Earth and the Moon together (5 Feb 2035)
records.summary: Seen from a point on Curiosity's route, for about 9.4 seconds.

records.title: An asteroid seen again after 19 years
records.summary: Sightings filed as 2007 VE138 and 2026 VV15 fit one orbit, and 2017 RB15 and 2026 RG39 connect across nine years. The 19-year orbit fits slightly better with a small outward push, but a later 59-position holdout favors gravity alone (2.506″ versus 3.103″ with the push). The two orbit programs use the same optical observations, so their agreement is not independent confirmation. Official identification rests with the Minor Planet Center.

records.title: Asteroid 2024 XS16 photographed fading into Earth's shadow (11 Dec 2024)
records.summary: A telescope in Sicily recorded the fade as the asteroid entered the shadow. The fade differs from a no-shadow prediction by only about 2.5 times its uncertainty.

records.title: Two asteroids that may have split apart about 1,800 years ago
records.summary: The orbits of (863192) 2014 SD315 and 2025 UC18 converge in the past.

records.title: Gaia's view of a spinning asteroid picks its shape
records.summary: The wobble of (664) Judith in Gaia's positions matches one of two published shape models.

records.title: An asteroid brushed past interstellar comet 2I/Borisov (28 Oct 2019)
records.summary: (704021) 2007 XJ8 passed about 106,000 km from Borisov, confirmed in telescope images.

records.title: The two pieces of comet 240P/NEAT are drifting apart
records.summary: The smaller fragment trails the larger by about 71 minutes of orbital motion.

records.title: A comet and an asteroid passed within 31,000 km (22 Feb 2026)
records.summary: Comet 407P/PANSTARRS–Fuls and asteroid (75547) 1999 XV257.

records.title: A comet lined up behind interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS (Oct 2025)
records.summary: 383P/Christensen and 3I/ATLAS lay on the same line out from the Sun on dates about a week apart. Whether any material from 3I reached 383P is unresolved.

records.title: The two bright knots of comet C/2020 P4-B
records.summary: Their separation is measured at 38.5 arcseconds. The discoverers first showed both knots in 2020.

records.title: An unexplained infrared excess in comet C/2025 R2 (SWAN)
records.summary: In single exposures from NASA's SPHEREx telescope the comet shows extra infrared light on 22 and 25 December 2025 and again on 2 January 2026. It is not a validated identification of any gas: calibration questions remain open, and a shape fitted to December failed to carry over to January.

records.title: No new sungrazing comets in 988 SOHO images
records.summary: A search for undiscovered members of the Kreutz comet family recovered only known comets.

records.title: No new interstellar body in a month of isolated survey tracklets
records.summary: No three-night high-speed link held up among 2,130 Pan-STARRS 1 tracklets. In a conditional synthetic-track test, 35 of 37 simulated paths near timed real sky detections linked correctly; detector footprints, brightness, encounter rate and 1,687 unresolved catalog entries remain unmeasured.

records.title: Repeated dips in two asteroids, but no confirmed moons
records.summary: TESS saw regular dimming of (29489) 1997 WQ and (3177) Chillicothe in 2018. Later visits did not show a steady rhythm.

records.title: Asteroid 2025 UQ146 keeps returning to Jupiter
records.summary: It was temporarily captured by Jupiter in 1984–1987 and should be again in 2069–2071.

records.title: ESA's JUICE will fly past an asteroid (25 Nov 2027)
records.summary: It should pass 49,751 km from (41013) 1999 UH22.

records.title: An infrared Planet Nine candidate did not reappear in public follow-up images
records.summary: A 2025 paper linked two far-infrared sources seen by IRAS in 1983 and AKARI in 2006. The old IRAS detector scans instead favour fixed sky emission, possibly from a nearby galaxy. DES and Euclid recovered 397/400 simulated dark planets (388/400 with perturbed historical positions), but uncertain AKARI timing and unmeasured regions prevent exclusion of the entire proposed orbit family.

records.title: Io's record 2024 eruption brightened Jupiter's sulfur glow but barely its sodium cloud
records.summary: Jupiter's sodium nebula and sulfur torus during Io's 2024 eruption-onset window

records.title: A 9.5-hour eclipse of Jupiter's moon Sinope (17–18 Oct 2037)
records.summary: The moon will sit far enough from Jupiter in our sky to be observed during the eclipse.

records.title: Saturn's rings will shade its moon Phoebe (1–3 Mar 2032)
records.summary: The B ring should twice remove about 98% of Phoebe's sunlight.

records.title: Saturn's A ring will pass in front of a radio source (28 Nov 2030)
records.summary: Some radio observatories will see it, even though the view from Earth's centre misses the ring.
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: Perdita appeared away from its predicted position in two JWST visits
records.summary: The known moon lay a median 0.50 and 1.17 arcseconds from the nominal JPL ephemeris. The observing team had previously reported a qualitative discrepancy; the two-visit circular fit has alternative orbit aliases.
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: Saturn's moon S/2023 S 38 probably has a gentler orbit than listed
records.summary: The discovery measurements favour the moderately stretched orbit its discoverers proposed over the extreme public solution.
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: Did Neptune's moon Nereid pass through Triton's shadow (31 Jan 2026)?
records.summary: Current JPL orbits say yes, while an older independent orbit says no. Archive images taken at that time could settle it.
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: Uranus's moons Umbriel and Ariel will eclipse three times in 22 hours (12–13 Mar 2050)
records.summary: Umbriel crosses Ariel and its sunlight three times in 22 hours
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: A 2006 crossing of the two moons of dwarf planet Haumea
records.summary: Orbit solutions place Hiʻiaka in front of Namaka on 13 Aug 2006, which archival images can test.
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: Two distant objects that may move in step with Neptune
records.summary: 2017 DO171 is a candidate member of Neptune's 8:1 resonance, using new Rubin Observatory positions. A second object is also a candidate.
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: The distant double object 2014 JR80 seen turning
records.summary: Five Rubin Observatory exposures on three nights in 2026 show the pair's orientation turning 49.46° in 11.963 days. With older images they favour a 103.03-day mutual orbit. Proudfoot and colleagues discovered that the object is double; the new part is the motion.
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: Solar Orbiter will see Venus hide Earth, then Jupiter (24 Dec 2026)
records.summary: Venus blocks Earth and Jupiter in succession during Solar Orbiter’s December 2026 flyby
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: Venus will pass in front of a pulsar (6 Feb 2027)
records.summary: PSR J1813−2113, as seen from the South Pole and New Zealand. A detection with current telescopes is not assured.
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: Venus and the pulsar PSR J1944−1750 (2 Mar 2054)
records.summary: Radio telescopes in South Africa and India could both see the occultation, if the pulsar's unmeasured motion is small.
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: A search for meteor flashes on Jupiter's night side found none
records.summary: Photon-by-photon data from the Juno spacecraft's ultraviolet instrument recover the flash published from 10 April 2020. A first frozen search of 2025 data found no trigger. Only three of the eight selected intervals held usable night-side photons, so this sets no impact rate.
records.topic: Planets, moons and rings in our Solar System

records.title: No new Earth-mass rogue planet in 10,971 public bulge light curves
records.summary: Several short or large-source brightenings survived screening, but blends and competing lens models prevent a confirmed planetary discovery. Without a monitored-star count, the search cannot measure how common rogue planets are.

records.title: A JWST search found no new wide planet around ten nearby stars
records.summary: Archive checks show that three apparent companions are previously recorded background sources. Contrast and injection tests describe only the searched parts of those images, not every possible companion.

records.title: Five more nearby stars checked for hidden planets with JWST
records.summary: No new companion was confirmed. One bright source proved to be a known background object and other peaks failed repeat-image checks; two faint signals still need deeper observations in later years to settle what they are.

records.title: Four "planets" that are really eclipsing stars
records.summary: TOI-3143.01's signal comes from the neighbouring binary TIC 384244835. A single eclipsing binary produced the two Kepler candidates KOI-7865.01 and KOI-7866.01. KOI-5275.01 is light from a binary 30 arcseconds away.

records.title: A neighbouring eclipsing binary shifts KELT-8 b's measured transit times
records.summary: An eclipsing binary shifts the apparent transit times of KELT-8 b

records.title: No sign of the proposed eighth TRAPPIST-1 planet
records.summary: JWST's dedicated observation shows no dip deeper than about 330 parts per million, while a transit at the shallow end of the proposal would usually have been detected.

records.title: Kepler-47 d will cross both of its suns at once (4 Jul 2029)
records.summary: For about 98 minutes the whole planet will sit inside both stellar disks.

records.title: Do the planets Kepler-18 c and d ever eclipse each other?
records.summary: Five transits in which both planets crossed their star test the planets' orbital orientation.

records.title: Kepler-359's apparent three-planet rhythm is not locked
records.summary: Most orbit solutions drift through all angles instead of staying locked in resonance.

records.title: Two Doppler signals at the nearby star HD 32564
records.summary: Signals at 2.56 and 11.06 days, fitted to older HARPS data, were recovered in new ESPRESSO velocities, making the star a low-mass companion candidate.

records.title: A "new" JWST source near ε Eridani was already in 2001 Keck images
records.summary: The positions match. The brightness comparison is in tension.

records.title: No additional transit candidate passed follow-up around 90 TESS hosts
records.summary: Three peaks survived the initial screen of 393 sector light curves. Stellar variability explained two, and the third reversed sign in a second photometric extraction.

records.title: Six planets listed more than four times too far from their stars
records.summary: The Open Exoplanet Catalogue's orbit sizes for the Kepler-445 and Kepler-446 planets were computed with the Sun's radius instead of each small star's own. Three more entries carry misplaced or mis-copied values, and the published orbit sizes of the four K2-285 planets do not fit a single star's mass.

records.title: A transit-like dip that flips sign
records.summary: On the flaring red dwarf TIC 257433294, a reported dip reappears in new TESS data but changes sign between two TESS data products, so its origin is uncertain.

records.title: A search for circularly polarised radio signals found known stars, not a new planet signal
records.summary: GJ 1151 and COCONUTS-2 A match previously published radio detections. Eleven nearby objects checked in available VLASS images showed no strong new signal; although many planet hosts lie within other surveys' image footprints, their individual radio limits are not yet measured.

records.title: No new unexplained deep dimmers in a TESS sector
records.summary: A search of 384 stars in Sector 105 (June–July 2026) found no validated irregular eclipses. A striking dimming toward TIC 316937197 repeats every 18.767 days, but which star in the close blend eclipses remains unknown. Recovery tests found 56% of 2%-deep, 12-hour dips; this single-sector search weakly constrains rare, multi-day events.

records.title: Gaia and LAMOST confirm a long binary orbit, not a dark companion
records.summary: Eighteen nights of independent spectra follow HD 264291 through its 1,007-day orbit. The inferred companion is 1.77 solar masses only under a no-companion-light model; two normal dwarfs are still possible. Another giant's inferred minimum crosses three solar masses when its stellar mass model changes. Neither case is an identified black hole or neutron star.

records.title: A high-speed star may escape the Milky Way
records.summary: DESI DR1 and Gaia DR3 give source 1717410430709663616 a Galactocentric speed of 697 km/s. All 4,096 draws escape in two reference Galactic potentials but remain bound in a heavier halo. The DESI velocity has only one epoch (binary motion untested), the modeled trajectory crosses the disk, but its origin remains open, and discovery priority remains open.

records.title: No verified laser-like emission in a targeted DESI DR1 stellar search
records.summary: All 10 persistent narrow residuals in 190 audited repeat-observed stars match the stellar Li I doublet; five independent-field stars reproduced a template false positive on separate nights. Per-star conditional laser-power limits are provided. This does not constrain unsearched fields or intermittent emitters.

records.title: No verified stellar waste heat in a small infrared sky survey
records.summary: SPHEREx and WISE found no qualifying excess around 404 nearby stars across 12.6 square degrees; published candidates remain affected by dusty galaxies, blends or unresolved mid-infrared emission. SPHEREx recovered none of the injected 100 K or 300 K excesses at 1% of stellar luminosity in its controls, so this is a limited null, not a Galaxy-wide constraint.

records.title: No new kind of infrared spectrum confirmed in two SPHEREx sky patches
records.summary: A search ranked 107 sources and flagged 57 for closer checks. Later observations could test 29 of those, and none retained an unexplained fitted feature; the other 28 lack complete comparisons. One bright spike did not repeat, and a real galaxy emission band matches a known type. These two patches cannot set an all-sky limit.

records.title: A candidate compact triple star
records.summary: In TIC 96100077 an eight-hour eclipsing pair sits at the position of a star with a 273-day Gaia orbit. Three ground surveys recover the predicted timing shifts.

records.title: Two eclipsing binaries drifting in opposite directions
records.summary: In TIC 140241924 one pair ran 42 minutes early and the other 51 minutes late in 2025, which supports their orbiting each other.

records.title: Both eclipses of binary A in TIC 43472931 arrived 9–11 minutes early
records.summary: Both eclipses of binary A in TIC 43472931 shifted earlier

records.title: An orbit that is slowly turning
records.summary: The secondary eclipse of TIC 35481236 moved 36 minutes within its orbit between 2018 and 2026.

records.title: A 20.27-hour rhythm and drifting eclipses in TIC 196989952
records.summary: The gap between its two eclipses grew by 3.24 hours over 16.7 years.

records.title: An ordinary eclipsing binary where a white-dwarf pair was proposed
records.summary: TIC 252468415 shows deep stellar eclipses every 3.166 days.

records.title: Two "double-double" star candidates
records.summary: Two pairs of eclipsing binaries share distances and motions on the sky.

records.title: CD−27 2812 may be a four-star system with a white dwarf
records.summary: CD−27 2812 and a candidate second binary

records.title: A cool star that changed speed by 367 km/s
records.summary: In STSP J153415.59+363616.8 a compact white-dwarf binary sits inside a group of four sources, making a candidate five-star system.

records.title: An asteroid's shadow split a star in two
records.summary: A 2022 occultation of HD 154615 revealed a close companion candidate to this eclipsing binary, whose eclipse timing is also changing.

records.title: A likely hidden third star in TYC 557-1335-1
records.summary: An asteroid occultation resolved two sources too far apart to share the star's known 59-day orbit.

records.title: A proposed dormant black hole with two visible stars
records.summary: TYC 2290-902-1 shows two sets of stellar lines and a 12.85-hour brightness cycle, a simpler explanation than a hidden black hole.

records.title: The published orbits of the triple star HD 73712 cannot all be right
records.summary: Two measured orbits give HD 73712 a hierarchy problem

records.title: An eclipse gap that grew by 6.96 hours
records.summary: The time between the two eclipses of OGLE-SMC-ECL-04602 widened over 25 years.

records.title: An eclipse gap that changed direction
records.summary: In OGLE-SMC-ECL-06090 a slowly turning orbit predicted later eclipse times within three minutes.

records.title: Eclipses that faded away and eclipses that deepened
records.summary: Both eclipses of OGLE-SMC-ECL-07730 faded while both eclipses of OGLE-SMC-ECL-06703 deepened.

records.title: A second dimming rhythm in OGLE-SMC-ECL-05439
records.summary: A 1.165-day cycle with alternating dips runs alongside the known binary.

records.title: Extra brightness signals near three Small Magellanic Cloud binaries
records.summary: Variations of 4.886 hours (toward 2dFS 757) and 4.252 hours (OGLE-SMC-ECL-01947), and a 12.72-hour dimming (OGLE-SMC-ECL-01293). The stars producing them are unresolved.

records.title: A steady 3.83-hour rhythm in the 2017 nova V612 Scuti
records.summary: A 3.8295-hour optical modulation at the position of V612 Scuti

records.title: A red giant that switched its pulsation from 137 days to 264 days
records.summary: In two other Mira stars, the dominant cycle shortened by 13% and 18%.

records.title: A Cepheid whose secondary pulsation comes and goes every 4.7 years
records.summary: OGLE-SMC-CEP-2332.

records.title: An RR Lyrae star that switched its main pulsation
records.summary: The new pulsation's period also grew by 44 seconds.

records.title: S Virginis swapped its bright and faint cycles around 2001
records.summary: A survey of 52,377 peaks in 510 Mira stars also dated a long alternating sequence in V Delphini. Earlier reports of alternation are credited.

records.title: β Pictoris's pulsations swapped strength between two TESS visits
records.summary: A reversal in the pulsation amplitudes of β Pictoris

records.title: Gaia19dyr went through a temporary phase of deep dips every 9 days
records.summary: A transient deep-dipping state in Gaia19dyr

A large flare on UX Arietis missing from flare catalogs (22 Oct 2021)
records.summary: It was seen in visible light by TESS and in X-rays by MAXI.

records.title: Clocks of 88 and 127 minutes in two X-ray-selected cataclysmic-variable candidates
records.summary: Two optical clocks in eROSITA cataclysmic-variable candidates

records.title: A 79-minute rhythm that persisted through a 2023 stellar outburst
Two helium emission lines that disagree in speed
records.summary: In SDSS J0903−0133 they differ by 67 km/s.

records.summary: A repeating infrared signal toward WR 117-2

records.title: A proposed one-day binary that is a sampling artifact
records.summary: The clock reported in the planetary nebula Al 2-R comes from the nightly observing pattern.

records.title: A "microlensing" source that keeps erupting
records.summary: K2C9-R-0367 (OGLE-2013-BLG-0769) brightened in at least six seasons, favouring a recurring stellar eruption over a one-time lens.

records.title: Radio counterparts to two exploding stars in our Galaxy
records.summary: Archival images show radio sources at the novae V1708 Sco and AT 2022sfe.

records.title: A methanol maser's 111-day cycle found in older data
records.summary: G28.011−0.426, recovered in 2009–2013 observations.

records.title: Frozen carbon dioxide along two sightlines near the nebula MN39
records.summary: SPHEREx sees deep CO₂-ice absorption, with absorption near water and carbon-monoxide ice as well. Foreground material is a plausible source.

records.title: A MeerKAT radio shell is a known planetary nebula
records.summary: G276.229+00.419 matches PHR J0942−5220 in shape and position.

records.title: Nineteen "galaxies" that are clouds in the Milky Way
records.summary: Nineteen entries in the FAST FASHI catalog of distant hydrogen sources come from four nebulae in our own Galaxy.

records.title: Two star clusters will pass within about 8 parsecs
records.summary: UPK 90 and UPK 93, in 2.6–3.5 million years.

records.title: Two planetary systems will pass about 10,000 au apart
records.summary: HD 34445 and HD 37124, in about 205,000 years.

records.title: A cold brown dwarf that could be weighed by its gravity
records.summary: WISE J2000+3629 will pass close to two background stars.

records.title: A star will nearly cover a quasar in June 2109

records.title: The black hole Gaia BH3 passed a star in 1928 and will pass two more

records.title: No new planet or debris transit confirmed around 42 bright white dwarfs
records.summary: In 39 uncrowded TESS targets, injections place a 95% upper limit of 11.13% on the fraction with a transiting companion 11.2 Earth radii in size on a 1.40794-day orbit. The fraction with planets at other orbital tilts, and the occurrence of irregular debris, remain unmeasured.

records.title: No faster supernova survivor found in the surveyed star catalogues
records.summary: None of 67,433 Gaia stars with well-measured parallaxes in four white-dwarf-oriented spectral catalogues had a measured sideways speed above 1,000 km/s. The all-sky speed cut missed 8 of 11 already known D⁶ white dwarfs, so this is a weak limit; one blended-looking fast star still needs follow-up.

records.title: Two white dwarfs with speed swings of about 250 km/s
records.summary: WD J0238+2733 and WD J0421−1325 are strong candidates for hidden companions.

records.title: Revised gravitational-wave clocks for eclipsing white-dwarf pairs
records.summary: Using the published parameters, ZTF J0720+6439's eclipses should drift about 13 seconds in 10 years rather than the 0.6 seconds stated in a preprint. Older survey data extend the eclipse record of seven pairs.

records.title: Calcium gas around WD J2307−0002 was already there 11 years earlier
records.summary: Broad calcium emission recurs at WD J230752.92−000207.45 across 4,002 days

records.title: A 16.35-hour period in the magnetic white dwarf WD 0140+130
records.summary: An earlier tentative 9.7-hour period is likely an alias of it.

records.title: Old images break a proposed regular cycle in WD J0923+7326
records.summary: Pan-STARRS shows bright states in 2010–2013 at the wrong times for the proposed recurrence.

records.title: A possible white dwarf that polluted the barium star HD 72223
records.summary: A faint companion 2,427 au away shares the system's distance and motion.

records.title: Wrong star IDs in a white-dwarf triples table
records.summary: Eleven Gaia identifiers in a published table point to the wrong member of ten systems.

records.title: A database listed titanium as nickel
records.summary: The fix changes which white dwarfs a published study selects. Debris at WD J2236−5548 is also measured as sodium-poor.

records.title: A search for cold neighbours of the Sun
records.summary: No previously unreported late-T or Y dwarf is validated by this search. In 84.80 deg² around the Euclid deep fields, two of 658 red CatWISE motion entries reproduced their tracks across five or more W2 epochs over at least five years and beat stationary and rotated tracks. Both are published dwarfs. A separate 4,235.10 deg² bright-source screen and a motion-first search found no new source with a secure cold spectrum and a parallax placing it within 20 pc.

records.title: SDSS-V DR20 changing-look pilot: calibration-limited development
records.summary: The 32-source cohort is frozen, but no changing-look classification has been tested or ruled out. Development calibration checks show substantial epoch-to-epoch differences. The preregistered broad-Hβ test cannot yet be applied defensibly: host and Fe II modeling, correlated noise and empirical false-change controls remain unqualified. The held-out spectra were opened for identity and exposure metadata only; their flux arrays were not examined.

records.title: Euclid development screen: no validated isolated candidate
records.summary: A bounded two-visit screen of a five-arcminute region in Euclid Deep Field North found two raw threshold crossings among 41 eligible compact-source tests. Inspection of the development images showed one crossing lies on a straight streak and the other is blended with a brighter neighbor. Neither is a validated isolated variable. The origin of the streak is unassigned. The third, later visit remains unopened. This result does not establish a variability rate, a survey sensitivity, or the absence of variables in the field.

records.title: Independent archival investigations, 15 November 2026
GOES-19 optical group decoding and a stereo direction check
records.summary: An independent native-file reader reproduced all 50,839 group records from six GOES-19 granules spanning 00:00–00:02 UTC on November 16, 2026. Of those, 50,361 have a decoded time within the two-minute window and 478 fall outside it. The quality flags classify 50,759 rows as good and 80 as degraded across all six files. These counts describe file-local groups, including any duplicates across granule boundaries. Physical flash counts and instrument livetime remain undetermined.

records.title: Resolved-satellite search: control fields and conditional sensitivity
records.summary: The DR11 search recovered the known Boötes I control but did not meet its joint spatial-and-distance recovery rule for Coma Berenices. One primary peak was retained, at Boötes I. A follow-up search outside 26 arcmin of the known controls retained zero peaks under its conditional shuffled-catalogue model; it was designed after the primary results and is exploratory. No new satellite or astrophysical survey null is established.

records.title: IMAP magnetic depletion screen
records.summary: No candidate passed the frozen five-minute screen. During the first 12 UTC hours of 2026-07-31, 133 of 144 five-minute bins passed magnetic-data quality and cadence gates. Of 142 overlapping three-bin comparisons, 127 had three valid bins and 103 had both controls at least 3 nT. None then met the required 1 nT drop below the mean of the two adjacent controls. The overlapping triplets are correlated; these counts are not independent trials. The result is limited to this cadence, scale, product, threshold and interval, and does not show that shorter or smaller magnetic depletions were absent.

records.title: Independent archival results
Independent archival findings
IXPE Mrk 501: a conditional repeatability screen
records.summary: The later 2026 IXPE observation did not cross the predeclared threshold for a change in the selected broadband Stokes vector. The fixed-center comparison gives Δ(q,u) = (0.04436484, −0.00885483), χ² = 0.88363247 and conditional p = 0.64286776. A predeclared XY-centroid sensitivity gives Δ(q,u) = (0.06147492, −0.01675437), χ² = 1.78333708 and p = 0.40997113. Both exceed the predeclared p threshold 5.7×10⁻⁷. The p-values are conditional on the stated statistical and calibration assumptions; this result does not establish physical constancy, a population limit, or a new discovery.

records.title: New independent lane: Mars Express VMC 2025-H2 global atmospheric transient search
records.summary: Status: prospective screening plan only; no discovery claim yet. Started 2026-11-15. This directory is deliberately new: it does not extend the existing Mars craters, impact timing, or spacecraft-geometry investigations. It does not use the SPHEREx moving-object lane in open PR #102.

records.title: MMS spacecraft 1 planar-boundary screen
records.summary: No candidate passed the frozen screen. In a 2026-09-30 MMS burst, 15,194 overlapping one-second windows had the required ten-second quality and cadence context; 11,125 also had both field endpoints at least 3 nT. None showed a rotation of 45° or more. These are overlapping windows, not independent trials. The largest eligible rotation was approximately 13.14°; that value is descriptive and did not set a new threshold. This is a bounded negative screen, not evidence that discontinuities or reconnection were absent.

records.title: The radial-velocity sample of NGC 1261b comes from Reticulum II
records.summary: All 12 stars with published radial velocities in the 70-star STREAMFINDER list for NGC 1261b are spectroscopic members or candidate members of the ultrafaint dwarf galaxy Reticulum II. All 12 match by exact Gaia source ID. Each was classified as a firm Reticulum II member by at least one of two spectroscopic studies. Removing these 12 stars leaves 58 candidates and zero published velocities for the branch in this atlas. The branch's apparent velocity concentration, 56.68–70.40 km/s with a median of 63.35 km/s, cannot provide independent spectroscopic evidence for tidal debris from the globular cluster NGC 1261.

records.title: NuSTAR clock-version comparison: calibration feasibility
records.summary: For the as-flown schedule envelope of Crab observation 11202302010, three public NuSTAR fine-clock solutions differ by microseconds. The observation is an identifying calendar window for a calibration comparison; no photon data, pulse phase, clock accuracy, coherence improvement or astrophysical finding was measured. The original selection and calculation were frozen in PROTOCOL.md and CALIBRATION_FREEZE.md. The results below are differences between solutions evaluated on the same dates, not independent observations.

records.title: PUNCH two-image development comparison
records.summary: Two 2026-11-01 PUNCH CTM v0l mosaics were compared in an authorized descriptive development run. The independently reproduced calculation retained 9,674,839 and 9,646,666 native eligible pixels, and 7,215,505 common pixels out of 16,777,216. The 64×64 block-mean difference contains 1,949 finite blocks. Grid and receipts document the calculation; the figure clips colors at the 98th percentile of absolute finite block values. This is not a front detection, physical flux change, significance test or absence claim.

records.title: Corrected sky positions for the SMGPS supernova-remnant image index
records.summary: The VizieR image table for Anderson et al. (2025) assigns displaced Galactic longitudes to the SARAO MeerKAT Galactic Plane Survey cutouts. The two coordinates labeled as the image center in the index differ from the center computed from the native FITS world coordinate system (WCS). coordinates.csv supplies the native center for each named file and identifies index positions that fall outside that same image. The affected product is J/A+A/693/A247/list. The original radio images and their native WCS remain usable. The corrected coordinates apply to file centers. The five separate source tables contain their own source-center measurements.

records.title: SO/PHI-FDT: a held-out radial-proxy persistence screen
records.summary: A fixed prediction for one magnetic-field proxy patch failed its two-scan holdout rule. The selected patch g42 increased by 8.659 G between two August 13, 2026 development scans. The frozen test required the same positive change, relative to its reference and control median, to exceed 3.236 G in each of two August 15 scans. The first held-out score was −9.846 G and failed; the second was +5.296 G and passed. Both were required, so the registered result is a non-replication.

records.title: Expanded optical TDE parent — metadata only
records.summary: This revises the 30-event pilot in ../vast-tde-metadata/; it does not replace or revise the original selection. Before reading radio fluxes, the author-published TDECat CSV was selected as an independently compiled optical TDE parent and a discovery date strictly before 2023-06-01 was specified. The 134 original rows and aliases are retained unchanged, 103 meet that date, and 31 later-discovered rows remain in the output as exclusions. The source authors document separate uncertain candidates in honourable_mentions.pdf; its exact original bytes are preserved at the D: campaign root, SHA-256 f79dc9823fcbf596de7d5756d828125eb1fc61add844cb16e6670779fa5a26b1. Those additional candidates are not silently treated as confirmed and need a separately frozen analysis if included. The parent CSV SHA-256 is cfda3e614c8f950daf693d469122a9019e5b41add186e69dbbc16d768e718a4a; it is distributed by its authors under CC BY-NC 4.0. TDECat is an incomplete compilation; the catalog CSV does not itself provide per-object spectral classifications, which must be verified in primary references before science testing.

records.title: Sealed VAST holdout packet — review only
records.summary: This extends the exact f323ab5 development packet; it does not alter it. Actual final sessions remain sealed until separate root review and authorization. holdout_cli.py checks the original manifest and code bytes, the exact development summary and all three development file hashes, plus a new reviewed code manifest and authorization record. The authorization must specify phase: holdout, authorized: true, the reviewed git_head, manifest_sha256, and development_summary_sha256. Only frozen control IDs and the two fixed sessions are eligible; failure produces an inconclusive record. Parquet predicates limit returned rows, not physical decoding of compressed column chunks.

records.title: VAST DR1 optical TDE metadata — proposed, not frozen
records.summary: Question: can pre-specified radio measurements provide evidence for a sustained late rise following an independently selected optical TDE? Observing unit: published optical event × uniquely associated VAST radio source × distinct image/visit. This is metadata-only; no radio flux, image pixels, or outcome-based selection have been inspected. No numerical test, threshold, or science selection is frozen by this draft.

records.title: Conditional VAST DR1 repeatability check for three TDE-candidate associations
records.summary: AT2020nov did not cross the frozen two-session rise screen. Its two held-out session comparisons were −0.705 and −0.057 model standard deviations relative to its development baseline. The known radio-variable control AT2018hyz crossed the same screen (3.342 and 4.111); the other known control, ASASSN-15oi, was below its baseline (−2.637 and −6.065). These are conditional comparisons of catalog peak fluxes, not calibrated physical significances or evidence of a new source.

records.title: NGC 7172: a within-visit iron-band count comparison
records.summary: The predeclared test found no significant change in the ratio of iron-band to nearby sideband counts between the two chronological halves of XRISM/Resolve observation 202074010. The ratios are 708/481 and 789/508; their ratio is 1.055 (approximate 95% interval 0.898–1.239), and the two-sided conditional Fisher test gives p=0.5384. These are observed counts, not calibrated astrophysical line fluxes. A non-significant test does not establish a constant line: the interval permits substantial changes, and the comparison is conditional on stable local continuum shape and background. The two halves are from the same visit and instrument.

spotlights.title: A week in a Martian particle storm
spotlights.subtitle: A particle surge in Martian orbit
spotlights.summary: MAVEN recorded a surge of energetic particles over 46 orbits around Mars.
spotlights.body: MAVEN measured unusually high fluxes of energetic ions and electrons from 22 to 29 August 2025. Across that window, 125 hours met the survey’s joint particle criteria. The peak hourly medians came on 24 August.

measurements.label: Peak ion flux / reference
measurements.method: Divide the August peak hourly median (157,000) by the survey median (30.55) for hours with at least 100 samples. Both fluxes are in (cm² s sr)⁻¹.

measurements.label: Peak electron flux / reference
measurements.method: Divide the August peak hourly median (616,500) by the survey median (25.2125) for hours with at least 100 samples. Both fluxes are in (cm² s sr)⁻¹.

measurements.label: Orbits with selected samples
measurements.method: Distinct spacecraft orbits with joint ion and electron samples in the selected hours.

spotlights.limitation: Forecasts for eruptions on both 20 and 21 August fit the timing. The source eruption remains uncertain. MAVEN measured particles in orbit, and the surface radiation dose remains unknown.

figure.caption: Each point is one August day's highest hourly median flux measured by MAVEN. Both species peaked on 24 August. The vertical scale is logarithmic.
figure.alt: MAVEN's daily peak electron and ion fluxes rise sharply on 23–24 August 2025 and decline through the following week.

spotlights.observingUnit: One UTC hour of MAVEN orbiter measurements. The survey reference uses 2,376 hours with at least 100 samples each.
spotlights.checked: Replaying all four survey files recovered the 46 orbits and both flux ratios. In the peak hour, all 450 timestamps matched the original NASA PDS Key Parameter table.
spotlights.nextTest: Compare calibrated particle energy spectra and shock timing against both candidate solar eruptions.

table.caption: Every observed UTC date in August 2025. Ions and electrons are the highest hourly median fluxes for each date, in (cm² s sr)⁻¹. Values retain the daily table’s precision.

measurements.label: Region 12847 angle offset
measurements.method: Project NOAA region 12847 from the 22 July summary into Solar Orbiter’s 13 July view and compare its direction with the X-ray centroid.

spotlights.limitation: The centroid is above the apparent limb. Its direction constrains the source more tightly than its longitude. Region 12847, or a source absent from the NOAA list, remains possible.

figure.caption: Solar Orbiter's science-pixel product shows a 15–25 keV hard X-ray pulse on 13 July 2021. Times are UTC at the spacecraft.
figure.alt: The 15–25 keV science count rate peaks near 286 counts per second at 18:27:38 spacecraft UTC.

spotlights.observingUnit: One published STIX flare centroid and a spacecraft-time X-ray light curve, compared with seven region centers in NOAA’s 22 July summary.
spotlights.checked: The two original STIX telemetry files reproduce the count-rate table. Projecting the NOAA centers gives the smallest angular offset for region 12849, followed by region 12847.
spotlights.nextTest: Reconstruct the X-ray image independently and identify the flare’s footpoint on the solar surface.

table.caption: All 15–25 keV science-product accumulations from 18:15 up to 18:45 on 13 July 2021. The times are measured at the spacecraft. Count rates are rounded to three decimals.

spotlights.title: A possible echo in a lensed quasar
spotlights.subtitle: Searching for a delay between images
spotlights.summary: The two quasar images show similar brightness changes. ZTF and Gaia correlation scans peak near seven months.
spotlights.body: Foreground gravity bends the quasar’s light along two paths. A detrended correlation scan places changes in the fainter northern image roughly seven months ahead of those in the brighter image. The numbers below are the best points on that scan’s five-day grid.

measurements.label: ZTF g-band scan peak
measurements.method: Peak of the detrended ZTF g-band correlation on a five-day grid, with image B leading A.

measurements.label: Gaia G-band scan peak
measurements.method: Same five-day search on independent Gaia G-band nights, with image B leading A.

measurements.label: Image separation
measurements.method: Great-circle distance between the listed A and B image coordinates.

spotlights.limitation: The latest held-out ZTF interval gave a slightly better predictive score at zero delay than at exactly 210 days. Uneven sampling and changes in each image’s brightness from microlensing leave the exact lag and its uncertainty open.

figure.caption: For comparison with image A, the upper panel shifts Gaia image B by +210 days and −1.94 magnitudes. The time shift comes from the ZTF scan peak. The lower panel shows changes in the ZTF images at their observed epochs.
figure.alt: Gaia light curves for the two lensed images line up after shifting by the ZTF delay. A second panel shows the long-term ZTF measurements.

spotlights.observingUnit: A night of brightness measurements in each quasar image. ZTF observed both images in g band and Gaia sampled an earlier interval in G band.
spotlights.checked: Independent reductions recovered all 2,121 published ZTF nights at printed precision and all 219 Gaia nights. Gaia’s sampled brightness peaks fall 202.90 days apart. Different models can favor lags of roughly 200–300 days.
spotlights.nextTest: Measure fresh, separately resolved flares in both images and test their predicted arrival times with a model fixed before the observations.

table.caption: All accepted Gaia G-band nights for images A and B. Each row retains its native epoch and measured magnitude before the horizontal and vertical offsets used in the figure.

spotlights.title: Does this radio source move with two dwarfs?
spotlights.subtitle: Following a pair of cold brown dwarfs
spotlights.summary: Radio peaks lie near the pair’s predicted positions in three visits. The second visit yielded a nondetection.
spotlights.body: Between 2017 and 2025 the fitted radio peak shifted northeast across the sky, close to the predicted motion of the brown-dwarf pair. In the 2020 image a beam fitted at the predicted position gave a flux consistent with local noise.

measurements.label: Radio centroid shift
measurements.method: Great-circle distance between the freely fitted radio centroids in October 2017 and September 2025.

measurements.label: Expected infrared shift
measurements.method: Displacement of the catalog proper-motion prediction between the same two radio visits.

measurements.label: 2020 fitted flux density
measurements.method: Beam fit at the predicted position in August 2020. Nearby control fits give a scatter of 0.15 mJy/beam.

spotlights.limitation: Two stationary sources whose brightness changes can also fit the images. The 2023 beam does little to separate them, and the 2017 quick-look image has known imaging caveats. The emitting object remains unidentified.

figure.caption: Four Very Large Array images share a sky grid and intensity scale. Cyan circles mark the predicted positions from infrared astrometry. The white cross marks the 2017 infrared prediction.
figure.alt: Radio peaks lie near the cyan circles in 2017, 2023 and 2025. The 2020 fit at the predicted position is consistent with noise.

spotlights.observingUnit: Four 2–4 GHz VLASS image cutouts. The motion compares the first and last visits. A pair of brown dwarfs fits inside one radio beam.
spotlights.checked: All four deposited FITS cutouts reproduce the fitted fluxes. Moving templates fit the two endpoint visits better than a source fixed at the low-frequency catalog position.
spotlights.nextTest: Observe the pair again when its predicted position is farther from both stationary alternatives. An image with a finer beam could separate the sources.

table.caption: All four VLASS visits. Flux is fitted at the predicted infrared position. Scatter comes from fits in nearby sky. The independent centroid fit is printed to six decimal places.
